document.title: Usama Bin Ladin: Charge Underscores U.S. Concerns on Interviews; Taliban Envoy Says Bin Ladin Hoodwinked Them and it Will Not Happen Again (Islama 09488)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] Taliban representative Syedur Rahman Haqqani says the Taliban allowed bin Laden to be interviewed so he could renounce terrorism, but he instead reiterated his commitment to attacking Americans and his right to use WMD. Haqqani promises no more interviews or terrorist activity, and says being 'tricked' did not change bin Laden's status as a guest.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Terrorist leader hosted as a 'guest' in Afghanistan; gave press interviews in December 1998

mentions.quote: BIN LADIN SAID IT WAS PERMISSIBLE TO ATTACK, LOOT, AND KILL U.S., U.K., AND ISRAELI CITIZENS.
THE PERTINENT FACT THAT BIN LADIN HAD TRICKED THEM DID NOT APPEAR TO AFFECT HIS STATUS IN AFGHANISTAN AS A "GUEST."
CHARGE MET DECEMBER 30 WITH LOCAL TALIBAN ENVOY SYEDUR RAHMAN HAQQANI
A NOTE DATED DECEMBER 15 SIGNED BY HAQQANI TO THE EFFECT THAT THE TALIBAN HAD BANNED BIN LADIN'S "PERSONAL ACTIVITIES"

persons.name: Alan Eastham
persons.role: US Chargé d'affaires (CDA), US Embassy Islamabad

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Taliban leader (Kandahar); gave interview disavowing Bin Ladin's statements

mentions.quote: MULLAH OMAR HAS GIVEN AN INTERVIEW IN WHICH HE SAYS THIS; IT WILL BE PUBLISHED TOMORROW
CHARGE ASKED THAT THIS QUESTION BE POSED TO KEY OMAR ASSISTANT MAULAWI WAKIL AHMED.

organizations.notes: Referred to as 'Bin Ladin and his network'.

events.description: US Chargé Eastham met Taliban envoy Syedur Rahman Haqqani to protest Bin Ladin's press interviews and warn the Taliban would be held accountable.
Haqqani signed a note to the US saying the Taliban had banned Bin Ladin's 'personal activities'.
Mullah Omar interview disavowing Bin Ladin's comments due to be published.
Reuters reported an unnamed Taliban official said Bin Ladin would not be expelled despite his interviews.
US Charge Alan Eastham met Taliban envoy Haqqani in Islamabad to protest bin Ladin's press interviews and demand Taliban accountability.
Taliban gave the US a note signed by Haqqani saying bin Ladin's 'personal activities' had been banned.
Reuters report cited an unnamed Taliban official saying bin Ladin would not be expelled despite his interviews.
Mullah Omar interview, due to be published, saying bin Ladin would be allowed no more interviews.
East Africa bombings, which bin Ladin said he personally supported, killed over 200 people.
Bin Ladin gave press interviews with Taliban permission, declaring attacks on US, UK and Israeli citizens permissible and asserting a right to WMD.

relationships.quote: CHARGE MET DECEMBER 30 WITH LOCAL TALIBAN REPRESENTATIVE SYEDUR RAHMAN HAQQANI
KEY OMAR ASSISTANT MAULAWI WAKIL AHMED

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin retains status as a 'guest' in Afghanistan despite the interviews.
relationships.quote: DID NOT APPEAR TO AFFECT HIS STATUS IN AFGHANISTAN AS A "GUEST."

relationships.detail: Referred to as head of 'Bin Ladin and his network'.
relationships.quote: ANY TERRORIST ATTACKS PERPETRATED BY BIN LADIN AND HIS NETWORK

relationships.detail: Haqqani is the local Taliban envoy/representative in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: CHARGE MET DECEMBER 30 WITH LOCAL TALIBAN REPRESENTATIVE SYEDUR RAHMAN HAQQANI

relationships.detail: Eastham is the Charge d'Affaires at US Embassy Islamabad, author of the cable.
Eastham sent the cable from Islamabad to SecState Washington.
relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD TO SECSTATE WASHDC IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is a 'guest' in Afghanistan under Taliban protection; Taliban reportedly would not expel him despite the interviews.
relationships.quote: DID NOT APPEAR TO AFFECT HIS STATUS IN AFGHANISTAN AS A "GUEST."

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin is residing in Afghanistan as a guest of the Taliban.
relationships.quote: HIS STATUS IN AFGHANISTAN AS A "GUEST."

relationships.detail: Bin Ladin denied involvement in, then said he personally supported, the East Africa bombings that killed over 200 people.
relationships.quote: HE THEN PROCEEDED TO SAY THAT HE PERSONALLY SUPPORTED THOSE BOMBINGS, WHICH KILLED OVER 200 PEOPLE.

relationships.detail: Taliban allowed bin Ladin to be interviewed to renounce terrorism, but he broke his promise; Taliban say he was hoodwinked them and will be barred from further interviews.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN HAD ALLOWED BIN LADIN TO BE INTERVIEWED SO THAT HE COULD RENOUNCE TBRRORISM, BUT HE HAD BROKEN HIS PROMISE

relationships.detail: Taliban repeatedly assured the US that bin Ladin was prevented from making threatening public statements.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN HAD REPEATEDLY ASSURED THE U.S. THAT BIN LADIN WAS BEING PREVENTED FROM MAKING PUBLIC STATEMENTS

relationships.detail: Wakil Ahmed is described as an assistant to Mullah Omar (rendered 'Key Omar').
relationships.quote: POSED TO KEY OMAR ASSISTANT MAULAWI WAKIL AHMED.

relationships.detail: Mullah Omar is the Taliban leader, giving an interview stating bin Ladin would not be allowed more interviews.
relationships.quote: MULLAH OMAR HAS GIVEN AN INTERVIEW IN WHICH HE SAYS THIS; IT WILL BE PUBLISHED TOMORROW

relationships.detail: Haqqani will relay the US message to Kandahar, the Taliban leadership seat.
relationships.quote: HAQQANI WILL GET OUR MESSAGE TO KANDAHAR

relationships.detail: Taliban reported a letter that groups operating out of Mashhad (Iran) may try to attack the US.
relationships.quote: GROUPS OPERATING OUT OF MASHHAD (TRAN) MAY TRY TO ATTACK THE U.S.

relationships.detail: The US refers to bin Ladin and his network as responsible for terrorist attacks.
relationships.quote: ANY TERRORIST ATTACKS PERPETRATED BY BIN LADIN AND HIS NETWORK

key_claims: The US held the Taliban accountable for any terrorist attacks by Bin Ladin and his network.
Haqqani admitted the Taliban allowed Bin Ladin's interviews so he could renounce terrorism but he broke his promise.
Haqqani promised no further interviews or public statements by Bin Ladin.
The Chargé doubted the Taliban would take concrete action beyond keeping Bin Ladin out of the public eye.
Bin Ladin's status as a Taliban 'guest' was unaffected, and a Taliban official said he would not be expelled.
Haqqani pointed to a Taliban-reported plot by groups in Mashhad, Iran against the US.
